cold_email.subject: Interest in Bioinformatics Consultant — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear n2 Group Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Bioinformatics Consultant opportunity with n2 Group at n2 Group.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Research Associate 1 (Temporary) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear SLAS (Society for Laboratory Automation and Screening) Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Research Associate 1 (Temporary) opportunity with SLAS (Society for Laboratory Automation and Screening) at SLAS (Society for Laboratory Automation and Screening).

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Orthotic Assistant/Athletic Trainer — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear OP Specialty Bracing Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Orthotic Assistant/Athletic Trainer opportunity with OP Specialty Bracing at OP Specialty Bracing.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.body:
Dear Michael Foods Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the QA Lab Tech-Nights opportunity with Michael Foods at Michael Foods.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. Dear Indiana State University Federal Credit Union Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Teller opportunity with Indiana State University Federal Credit Union at Indiana State University Federal Credit Union.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Cal Coast Student Financial Center - Trainee (Student Services Professional I/A) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Fowler College of Business at San Diego State University Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Cal Coast Student Financial Center - Trainee (Student Services Professional I/A) opportunity with Fowler College of Business at San Diego State University at Fowler College of Business at San Diego State University.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Social Media Manager — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Dartcor Hospitality Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Social Media Manager opportunity with Dartcor Hospitality at Dartcor Hospitality.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Wellness Coach (100% Remote) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear ClearCaptions, LLC Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Wellness Coach (100% Remote) opportunity with ClearCaptions, LLC at ClearCaptions, LLC.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Assistant Teacher — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear The Growing Years, Australia Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Assistant Teacher opportunity with The Growing Years, Australia at The Growing Years, Australia.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Regional Advancement Officer- San Francisco Bay Area — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Purdue for Life Foundation Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Regional Advancement Officer- San Francisco Bay Area opportunity with Purdue for Life Foundation at Purdue for Life Foundation.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

Dear MaineHealth Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. cold_email.subject: Interest in Instructional Technology Support Specialist — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear HCA Healthcare Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Instructional Technology Support Specialist opportunity with HCA Healthcare at HCA Healthcare.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Research Assistant, FACE Lab — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Emerson College Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Research Assistant, FACE Lab opportunity with Emerson College at Emerson College.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.body:
Dear American Enterprise Institute Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the HR Assistant/Coordinator opportunity with American Enterprise Institute at American Enterprise Institute.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Admissions Counselor II - Houston — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Texas A&M AgriLife Center for Managed Technology Services Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Admissions Counselor II - Houston opportunity with Texas A&M AgriLife Center for Managed Technology Services at Texas A&M AgriLife Center for Managed Technology Services.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Client Service Coordinator Campus Plaza — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Banfield Pet Hospital Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Client Service Coordinator Campus Plaza opportunity with Banfield Pet Hospital at Banfield Pet Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.description: Career Category Clinical Job Description Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do. Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline and portfolio of medicines to treat heart disease, obesity and obesity-related conditions, rare diseases, inflammatory conditions and cancer. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives. Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career. Biostatistical Programming Manager What you will do Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. In this vital role you will report to a Sr. Manager in CfOR’s Data & Analytic Center. This role will support the CfOR organization by setting goals with CfOR epidemiologists, laying out a strategy to deliver on those goals, and coordinating with a functional service provider (FSP)-based team of contract programmers to achieve the goals. In addition, the Manager is responsible for staying informed of evolving department needs and industry best practices, identifying innovative, impactful proposals to increase efficiency, and supporting the organization’s growth strategies. Responsibilities Lead an FSP-based programming team conducting analyses supporting CfOR’s Data & Analytic Center Coordinate with functional leads to prioritize and manage workflow Identify potential efficiency improvements and propose solutions Collaborate with CfOR FSP liaison to ensure performance and quality standards from FSP-based programming team Ensure the analysis and presentation of biomedical data is accurate and complete Adhere to Amgen policies, SOPs and other controlled documents Write, test, and validate programs in SAS, Databricks, or R Efficiently manage FSP-based programming team to deliver on time and to specifications Review and approve key study-related documents produced by other functions, e.g. SAPs, Data Management Plans, etc. Write and/or review and approve programming plans and analysis dataset specifications Represent the programming function and participate in multidisciplinary team meetings Contribute to the continuous improvement of programming, CfOR, and Research and Development (R&D) Write, test and validate department-, product- and protocol-level macros and utilities Participate in intra-departmental and CfOR meetings Support and mentor junior programmers What we expect of you We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The professional we seek is a Biostatistical Programming Manager with these qualifications. Basic Qualifications Doctorate degree OR Master’s degree and 2 years of experience OR Bachelor’s degree and 4 years of experience OR Associate’s degree and 8 years of experience OR High school diploma / GED and 10 years of experience Preferred Qualifications Master’s degree in Epidemiology, Biostatistics, or other subject with high statistical content Vendor relationship management or related experience with functional service providers Experience with real world healthcare data such as MarketScan, Optum, Komodo, Medicare and EMR databases Pharmaceutical industry experience Database programming using SQL Minimum five years SAS programming experience Experience with advanced statistical methods such as survival and regression analysis Key Competencies Programming with SAS, R, SQL, Python or other procedural languages Technical excellence Leadership Innovation Project management Teamwork Problem solving Attention to detail Oral and written communication Understanding of computer operating systems, including cloud-based (AWS), Databricks and UNIX What you can expect from us As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. cold_email.subject: Interest in Biostatistical Programming Manager — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Amgen Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Biostatistical Programming Manager opportunity with Amgen at Amgen.

I am especially interested in building scalable data systems that let research and clinical teams use biological data reliably. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, I have built API-driven and Snakemake-based pipelines, automated SQL workflows, and worked across both scientific and software contexts.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.description: Associate Scientist, Immunology Why Patients Need You Pfizer’s purpose is to deliver breakthroughs that change patients’ lives. Research and Development is at the heart of fulfilling this mission as we translate advanced science into therapies and vaccines that matter most. As part of the Cell-Mediated Immunoassays (CMI) group, you will contribute to understanding immune responses that drive vaccine efficacy and safety. What You Will Achieve As an Associate Scientist in the CMI group, you will play a critical role in generating high-quality cellular immunology data to support Pfizer’s clinical vaccine programs. The primary focus of this role is to execute clinical assays, primarily flow cytometry, with the potential to support additional assays such as ELISPOT and ADCC. Beyond routine testing, you will help drive operational excellence by applying 5S, automation, and process optimization to strengthen laboratory workflows. How You Will Achieve It Perform high-throughput flow cytometry assays to characterize cellular immune responses Support additional cellular immunoassays such as ELISPOT and ADCC as needed. Maintain compliance with GxP and internal SOPs for all laboratory activities Support the qualification of new assays and ensure accurate documentation of experimental work Drive operational improvements, including 5S, laboratory automation, and process optimization, to increase the efficiency and robustness of testing workflows Help uphold quality and compliance across CMI through sound documentation practices, data integrity, and audit-readiness Prepare reagents, maintain inventory, and manage sample workflows efficiently Analyze and interpret assay results and present findings to team members and leadership Collaborate within the CMI group and cross-functionally to support vaccine development programs Qualifications Must-Have Bachelor's degree in a relevant scientific discipline w/ 0+ to 2 years of experience. Hands-on laboratory experience in immunology or a related field Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment Ability to manage multiple priorities and adapt to changing business needs Scientific curiosity and a desire to continuously learn and expand technical expertise Experience using common AI tools, including generative technologies such as ChatGPT or Microsoft Copilot, to support problem solving and enhance productivity. Demonstrated curiosity for exploring how these tools can improve outcomes and understanding of responsible AI practices, including risk management and ethical use. Nice-to-Have Experience with flow cytometry and understanding of its scientific principles Knowledge of immunology and cellular immune responses Familiarity with ELISPOT, ADCC or other biofunctional assays Understanding of relevant statistics and data analysis Experience with laboratory automation and high-throughput workflows Experience with continuous improvement or Lean methodologies (e.g., 5S) Familiarity with LIMS or other electronic laboratory systems Exposure to mammalian cell culture and aseptic techniques Prior experience in a clinical or regulated laboratory environment AI fluency, with interest in applying AI and digital tools to workflows Work Location Assignment: On Premise The annual base salary for this position ranges from $60,200.00 to $100,400.00. jobs.title: Staff Systems Support Engineer
jobs.description: What if the work you did every day could impact the lives of people you know? Or all of humanity? At Illumina, we are expanding access to genomic technology to realize health equity for billions of people around the world. Our efforts enable life-changing discoveries that are transforming human health through the early detection and diagnosis of diseases and new treatment options for patients. Working at Illumina means being part of something bigger than yourself. Every person, in every role, has the opportunity to make a difference. Surrounded by extraordinary people, inspiring leaders, and world changing projects, you will do more and become more than you ever thought possible. Staff Systems Support Engineer Cambridge - Onsite As a Staff Systems Support Engineer , you will join our Global Lab Management team and play a critical role in supporting the development of next-generation sequencing technologies. Working at the intersection of hardware, software, engineering, and science, you will help ensure our sequencing instrument fleet operates at the highest standards, empowering R&D teams to deliver the innovations that shape the future of genomics. Why Illumina? At Illumina, you'll work alongside experts across disciplines, contribute to meaningful and innovative projects, and continuously grow through new challenges and experiences. Our culture is built on collaboration, curiosity, and a shared commitment to making an impact. This is an opportunity to: Support cutting-edge sequencing technologies at the forefront of genomics innovation. Partner with world-class Chemistry, Software, Consumables, Engineering, and Integration teams. Solve complex technical challenges that directly enable scientific breakthroughs. Work in a collaborative, international environment where every contribution matters. Build your expertise while helping advance technologies that improve human health. The Role As a Staff Systems Support Engineer, you will work closely with Illumina's R&D teams to ensure the sequencing instrument fleet is operational, reliable, and capable of supporting critical development activities. You will leverage your technical expertise across hardware, software, firmware, and systems troubleshooting to maximize instrument performance and enable innovation. What You'll Do Troubleshoot and resolve issues on sequencing instruments to support research and development activities. Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to ensure instruments are fit for purpose, including implementing hardware and software modifications where required. Monitor instrument performance through sequencing data analysis and execute preventative maintenance and upgrade activities. Partner with EERD and Systems Integration teams to maintain fleet availability and operational excellence. Support, mentor, and provide technical guidance to junior team members. Develop and communicate key performance metrics, including failure analysis and Pareto reporting. Provide timely, clear communication to users regarding investigations, corrective actions, and repair timelines. Collaborate with global instrument and software development teams, including colleagues in the United States, to support software, firmware, and hardware upgrades. Represent the engineering support function on project teams requiring sequencing instrument expertise. What You'll Bring Required Qualifications & Experience Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Bioinformatics, Physical Sciences, or a related discipline. Significant experience supporting complex opto-electronic systems in a commercial or R&D environment. Strong troubleshooting capability across integrated hardware, firmware, and software systems. Coding experience and hands-on experience working with Linux operating systems. Experience troubleshooting and diagnosing PCB-level issues. Strong communication skills with the ability to convey technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences. Ability to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment and manage competing priorities. Preferred Experience Experience working with sequencing instrumentation or related life science technologies. Knowledge of enterprise processes and tools such as Jira, Jama, and Confluence. Experience working within cross-functional and geographically distributed teams. The estimated base salary range for the Staff Systems Support Engineer role based in United Kingdom is GBP 69,500 - 104,300. The range reflects long‑term growth in the role; therefore, most candidates are hired between the minimum and middle of the range. Placement depends on experience, skills, location, and internal equity. This salary range applies to the primary posting location listed above. Should the level or location of the role change during the hiring process, the applicable base pay range will be updated accordingly. Compensation ranges for other locations will differ to reflect local market competitiveness and will be shared with candidates if applicable during the recruitment process. Additionally, all employees are eligible for one of our variable cash programs (bonus or commission) and eligible roles may receive equity as part of the compensation package. We offer a thoughtfully designed benefits package that supports your wellbeing, flexibility, and life beyond work—combining globally differentiated offerings with locally tailored programs. This includes support during important life moments, flexible time off, opportunities to give back, and a weeklong company-wide summer shutdown. In the UK, we also offer flexible benefits, a company contribution of 10% into your pension, and private medical insurance, alongside additional benefits to support you and your family. We are a company deeply rooted in belonging, promoting an inclusive environment where employees feel valued and empowered to contribute to our mission. Built on a strong foundation, Illumina has always prioritized openness, collaboration, and seeking alternative perspectives to propel innovation in genomics. We are proud to confirm a zero-net gap in pay, regardless of gender, ethnicity, or race. We also have several Employee Resource Groups (ERG) that deliver career development experiences, increase cultural awareness, and offer opportunities to engage in social responsibility. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer committed to providing employment opportunity regardless of sex, race, creed, color, gender, religion, marital status, domestic partner status, age, national origin or ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, sexual orientation, pregnancy, military or veteran status, citizenship status, and genetic information. Illumina conducts background checks on applicants for whom a conditional offer of employment has been made. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with applicable local, state, and federal laws. Background check results may potentially result in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment. The background check process and any decisions made as a result shall be made in accordance with all applicable local, state, and federal laws. Illumina prohibits the use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in the application and interview process. If you require accommodation to complete the application or interview process, please contact accommodations@illumina.com. To learn more, visit: https://www.dol.gov/ofccp/regs/compliance/posters/pdf/eeopost.pdf. The position will be posted until a final candidate is selected or the requisition has a sufficient number of qualified applicants. This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

cold_email.subject: Interest in Staff Systems Support Engineer — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Illumina Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Staff Systems Support Engineer opportunity with Illumina at Illumina.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

cold_email.subject: Interest in Lead Children Development Coach or Instructor — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear The Little Gym International Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Lead Children Development Coach or Instructor opportunity with The Little Gym International at The Little Gym International.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: Applied AI Analyst II
jobs.description: At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. The Applied AI Analyst II, Enabling Functions will help evolve Enabling Functions Analytics from static reporting toward intelligent, conversational, and reusable analytics products. The role combines practical AI research, context engineering, semantic modelling, and hands-on prototyping to connect governed enterprise data with large language models and modern analytics platforms. The individual will investigate how LLMs process context and generate responses, translate those learnings into reliable solution patterns, and build AI-enabled experiences using Claude, Databricks, Power BI, and related technologies. The role includes building text-to-SQL workflows, tool-using agents, and multi-agent systems that answer business questions reliably and transparently Roles & Responsibilities Apply working knowledge of concepts and procedures to a variety of analytics and AI assignments, using judgement to solve problems with a moderate level of guidance. Own well-defined research, experimentation, and prototyping workstreams, documenting assumptions, decisions, results, and limitations. Research and test LLM behaviours, reasoning patterns, context-window usage, tool use, structured outputs, and failure modes, and convert findings into practical design guidance and reusable patterns for analytics use cases. Design and optimise system instructions, business context, examples, metadata, retrieval strategies, and tool interfaces so AI responses are grounded, relevant, and consistent. Manage context quality, freshness, and token efficiency. Build text-to-SQL workflows that translate natural-language questions into governed queries, grounded in certified semantic models and metric definitions, with validation steps that check generated SQL before execution. Design tool-using agents that call approved functions and data services (such as SQL execution, metric lookup, and visualization generation) with clearly defined tool schemas, permissions, and fallback behaviour. Design and prototype multi-agent workflows in which specialist agents (for example, query planning, SQL generation, validation, and insight narration) coordinate under an orchestrator, with clear handoffs, state management, and loop and cost limits. Prototype chat-with-data and chat-with-document experiences that let users explore governed business information in natural language, while preserving traceability to approved data and metric definitions. Design and improve business-ready semantic models covering grain, dimensions, measures, relationships, hierarchies, synonyms, descriptions, and certified definitions, ensuring the same logic supports Power BI, Databricks, and AI experiences. Evaluate when to use prompting, retrieval-augmented generation, tool calling, multi-agent workflows, or traditional analytics, and define fit-for-purpose architectures rather than applying LLMs where deterministic methods are more appropriate. Create test cases and evaluation datasets for SQL accuracy, tool-call correctness, agent task completion, groundedness, latency, and cost. Investigate hallucinations, retrieval or semantic failures, and agent loops, and recommend corrective actions. Build proof-of-value solutions using Python, SQL, APIs, Claude, and Databricks, integrating AI capabilities with existing analytics assets and, where appropriate, Power BI or lightweight application experiences. Break ambiguous business questions into clear problem statements, hypotheses, data needs, and solution options. Rapidly learn unfamiliar domains and communicate trade-offs to technical and non-technical stakeholders. Document patterns, reusable components, guardrails, and lessons learned, and contribute to internal standards for context engineering, semantic models, LLM evaluation, and responsible AI adoption. Partner with business analysts, BI developers, data engineers, AI/ML specialists, architects, and governance teams to move successful prototypes toward sustainable products. Balance innovation with responsible AI, data governance, security, privacy, quality, and production-readiness expectations, including human-in-the-loop controls for consequential actions. Skills and competencies Strong analytical thinking, curiosity, and structured problem-solving, including comfort with ambiguous questions and incomplete information. Practical understanding of how large language models work, including tokenisation, embeddings, attention, context windows, inference, common failure modes, and the difference between model knowledge and supplied context. Hands-on expertise in prompt and context engineering, including instruction design, few-shot examples, grounding, retrieval-augmented generation, structured outputs, tool use, and context optimisation. Strong SQL workflow skills: writing and reviewing complex queries, designing text-to-SQL pipelines, enforcing read-only access and query guardrails, validating generated SQL against schema and metric definitions, and diagnosing incorrect joins, grain mismatches, and aggregation errors. Experience designing tool-using agents, including function and tool schema design, argument validation, error handling, retries, and permission boundaries. Working knowledge of multi-agent architectures such as orchestrator-worker, planner-executor, and specialist-agent patterns, including state management, handoffs between agents, termination conditions, and observability across agent steps. Hands-on experience with Anthropic Claude or comparable enterprise LLM platforms, including API-based integration, prompt orchestration, tool calling, and solution evaluation. Hands-on experience with Databricks, including notebooks, SQL Warehouses, governed data assets, and lakehouse-based analytics workflows. Exposure to Unity Catalog, AI/BI Genie, MLflow, or Mosaic AI is valuable. Experience designing and integrating REST APIs or equivalent service interfaces to connect LLMs, enterprise data platforms, and application experiences. Proficiency in Python and SQL for data exploration, AI prototyping, integration, evaluation, and automation. Experience with Git-based source control, branching, and pull-request practices, together with CI/CD pipelines for automated build, test, and deployment Hands-on understanding of AWS deployment patterns for AI and analytics solutions, including environment configuration, security, logging, monitoring, and release processes is a plus Experience designing or consuming semantic models, with strong understanding of business metrics, dimensional modelling, relationships, grain, hierarchies, synonyms, and reusable business definitions. Experience with vector search, agent frameworks, Model Context Protocol, LLM observability, or automated evaluation methods. Ability to design experiments and evaluation datasets and assess groundedness, relevance, consistency, completeness, latency, and cost. Ability to present complex information to non-technical stakeholders in a clear and concise manner, and to create relevant and engaging PowerPoint presentations. Awareness of responsible AI, privacy, cybersecurity, data governance, access control, and human-in-the-loop controls. Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to translate technical AI concepts into practical business implications and document reusable engineering patterns. Ability to work collaboratively in cross-functional teams and manage multiple projects simultaneously. Good to Have Practical machine learning knowledge, including supervised and unsupervised learning, feature engineering, model evaluation, and basic MLOps. Experience with Power BI, including semantic models, DAX, Power Query, row-level security, and integration of BI assets with AI-enabled analytics experiences. Familiarity with React or lightweight full-stack application development for creating user-facing AI experiences. Experience with agent orchestration frameworks and production monitoring of multi-agent systems. Experience working in regulated or highly governed enterprise environments. Experience Bachelor's or master's degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Engineering Approximately 3–5 years of relevant experience in analytics, data science, AI engineering, software engineering, or a closely related field. Strong applied project work may substitute for some formal experience. Demonstrated experience solving analytical problems using Python and SQL, including building or reviewing text-to-SQL or query-generation workflows. Demonstrated hands-on delivery involving Claude or a comparable LLM, tool-using agents or multi-agent workflows, Databricks, APIs, Git/CI/CD, and deployment of an AI-enabled analytics prototype. Experience working with stakeholders to translate a business question into a testable analytical or AI solution. Experience producing clear technical documentation and communicating analytical results using compelling oral and written storytelling. Ability to handle, and maintain the confidentiality of, highly sensitive information. We hire for skills and capabilities, not just credentials – if this role excites you, but doesn’t perfectly match your resume, we encourage you to apply anyway. cold_email.subject: Interest in Applied AI Analyst II — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Bristol Myers Squibb Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Applied AI Analyst II opportunity with Bristol Myers Squibb at Bristol Myers Squibb.

I am especially interested in building scalable data systems that let research and clinical teams use biological data reliably. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, I have built API-driven and Snakemake-based pipelines, automated SQL workflows, and worked across both scientific and software contexts.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: Analyst - US Commercialization Decision Intelligence & MMx Solutions
jobs.description: At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. BMS Hyderabad is an integrated global hub where our work is focused on helping patients prevail over serious diseases by building sustainable and innovative solutions. This important science, technology, and innovation center will support a range of technology and drug development activities that will help us usher in the next wave of innovation. Decision Analyst I Summary: The Decision Analyst will play an instrumental role for BMS, as they will be responsible for applying advanced statistical analysis and optimization techniques to support data-driven decision-making processes. The Decision Analyst will develop and implement descriptive/explanatory models, decision support models, segmentation strategies, portfolio analyses, test/experimental designs, and measurement frameworks to provide actionable insights and recommendations that enhance business performance and drive growth in the region. Roles & Responsibilities Analytics Delivery & AI Enablement Support the development and delivery of analytical solutions under the guidance of senior analysts and team leads. Apply foundational analytics, decision science, and AI/ML techniques to support US Commercial initiatives across brand strategy, omnichannel engagement, and resource allocation. Translate well-defined business questions into analytical tasks, execute analyses, and summarize findings. Ensure accuracy, quality, and adherence to analytical best practices in all deliverables. Stakeholder Support & Business Understanding Collaborate with US Commercial stakeholders, Global Analytics, OCx, Marketing, and BIT to understand business context and analytical requirements. Support preparation of analytical outputs, presentations, and dashboards for stakeholder discussions. Clearly communicate results, assumptions, and limitations with guidance from senior team members. Incorporate stakeholder feedback to refine analyses and outputs. Omnichannel & Commercial Analytics Execute analytics supporting personal and non-personal promotion channels, including field force, email, web, paid media, social, and third-party platforms. Support development and tracking of performance metrics related to reach, engagement, and effectiveness. Assist in test-and-learn initiatives, A/B tests, and basic quasi-experimental analyses. Identify trends, anomalies, and opportunities in data and escalate insights to senior team members. Team Collaboration & Learning Work collaboratively within project teams, contributing to shared goals and timelines. Learn and adopt standard analytical frameworks, tools, and coding best practices used by the team. Participate in knowledge-sharing sessions, training programs, and peer reviews. Demonstrate curiosity and initiative in developing analytical and business skills. Technical Execution & Data Handling Build and maintain datasets, basic models, dashboards, and recurring reports. Perform data validation, quality checks, and documentation of analytical processes. Work with data engineering and BIT teams to understand data structures and resolve data issues. Follow established governance, compliance, and documentation standards. Skills & Competencies Strong analytical mindset with attention to detail and data quality. Good written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain analyses in simple terms. Ability to manage assigned tasks effectively and meet deadlines. Willingness to learn new tools, techniques, and business concepts. Collaborative and proactive team player with a positive attitude. Basic problem-solving skills and ability to apply structured thinking. Experience & Qualifications BA/BS required; degrees in life sciences, computer science, mathematics, statistics, data science, or engineering preferred. 1–3 years of professional experience in analytics, data analysis, decision science, or related roles. Experience working with structured datasets and performing quantitative analyses. Exposure to commercial analytics, marketing analytics, or healthcare/pharmaceutical analytics is a plus. Interest in applying data, analytics, and AI to solve real-world business problems. Technical Skills (Preferred) Hands-on experience with Python and/or R for data analysis and basic modelling. Familiarity with statistical concepts and introductory machine learning techniques. Experience with data visualization and reporting tools (e.g., R Shiny, Dash, Tableau, Power BI, or similar). Exposure to collaborative analytics environments (e.g., Databricks, Git, SharePoint). Basic understanding of omnichannel, digital marketing, or commercial data sources. We hire for skills and capabilities, not just credentials – if this role excites you, but doesn’t perfectly match your resume, we encourage you to apply anyway. How We Work Where you work matters – because collaboration, innovation and patient impact happen in many settings. Our roles are structured across four work models: site-essential, site-by-design, field-based and remote-by-design. The model assigned to this role is based on its core responsibilities. Learn more at https://careers.bms.com/ways-of-working. Supporting People with Disabilities BMS is dedicated to ensuring that people with disabilities can excel through a transparent recruitment process, reasonable workplace accommodations/adjustments and ongoing support in their roles. Applicants can request a reasonable workplace accommodation/adjustment prior to accepting a job offer. cold_email.subject: Interest in Analyst - US Commercialization Decision Intelligence & MMx Solutions — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Bristol Myers Squibb Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Analyst - US Commercialization Decision Intelligence & MMx Solutions opportunity with Bristol Myers Squibb at Bristol Myers Squibb.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: Business Development Operations Associate
jobs.description: ABOUT FORMATION BIO Formation Bio is a tech and AI driven pharma company differentiated by radically more efficient drug development. Advancements in AI and drug discovery are creating more candidate drugs than the industry can progress because of the high cost and time of clinical trials. Recognizing that this development bottleneck may ultimately limit the number of new medicines that can reach patients, Formation Bio, founded in 2016 as TrialSpark Inc., has built technology platforms, processes, and capabilities to accelerate all aspects of drug development and clinical trials. Formation Bio partners, acquires, or in-licenses drugs from pharma companies, research organizations, and biotechs to develop programs past clinical proof of concept and beyond, ultimately helping to bring new medicines to patients. The company is backed by investors across pharma and tech, including a16z, Sequoia, Sanofi, Thrive Capital, John Doerr, Spark Capital, SV Angel Growth, and others. You can read more at the following links: - Our Vision for AI in Pharma https://www.formation.bio/blog/our-vision-for-ai-in-pharma - Our Current Drug Portfolio https://www.formation.bio/licensing-and-pipeline - Our Technology & Platform https://www.formation.bio/technology At Formation Bio, our values are the driving force behind our mission to revolutionize the pharma industry. Every team and individual at the company shares these same values, and every team and individual plays a key part in our mission to bring new treatments to patients faster and more efficiently. ABOUT THE POSITION This role keeps Business Development (BD) running and makes it run better. You will own the recurring workflows BD depends on, including project managing the end-to-end deal process across sourcing, diligence, negotiations, and contracting; the CRM, deal flow reporting, meeting cadence, the BD process, and the materials BD produces for leadership, the Board, and town halls. You will also propose and implement improvements, using AI wherever it can raise the speed and quality of BD's work. You will report to a Director, Business Development, and work closely with the broader BD team, Product, Tech, and BizOps. RESPONSIBILITIES - Own and maintain the BD process and its documentation as the team's work evolves - Propose and implement improvements to BD processes, tools, and workflows, with review from BD leadership for changes that affect the team, and track whether they work - Identify, test, and implement AI tools and automations that improve BD outcomes, and share what works with the team - Build and maintain reporting and dashboards on deal flow, pipeline stage, and team activity for BD leadership - Own the BD CRM, including data entry standards, upkeep, and data quality, and work with Tech and Product to improve its workflows - Coordinate agendas, materials, and follow-ups for standing, triage, and ad hoc BD meetings - Prepare first drafts of materials for BD leadership, the Board of Directors, quarterly town halls, and fund partners - Support cross-functional BD initiatives by tracking milestones, owners, and follow-through SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS - Strong organization, attention to detail, and reliability on recurring deadlines - Proficiency with the Microsoft Office suite, including Excel and PowerPoint - An aggressive AI adopter who is eager to implement AI in ways that improve BD outcomes, and comfortable testing new tools and building automations - Ability to design, improve, and clearly document processes - Strong written and verbal communication, including producing polished materials for senior audiences - Ability to manage competing requests and work cross-functionally with Product, Tech, BizOps, and R&D - Interest in biotech and pharma business development EXPERIENCE & EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS - 1-3 years of consulting, operations, or corporate strategy experience, preferably in the biotech/pharma industry; project management experience preferred - Bachelor's degree required, with strong focus in Biology or related scientific discipline preferred Total Compensation Range: $106,000 - $132,500 Compensation Individual compensation is determined by several factors, including role scope, geographic location, and skills & experience. Your offer will reflect where you fall within the range based on these considerations. In addition to base salary, we offer equity, comprehensive benefits, and generous perks. If the posted range doesn't match your expectations, we still encourage you to apply! Where We Hire Formation Bio is prioritizing hiring in key hubs, primarily the New York City and Boston metro areas, with a hybrid model requiring 3 days per week in office. Applicants from the Research Triangle (NC) and San Francisco Bay Area may also be considered. Please apply only if you reside in these locations or are willing to relocate. Equal Opportunity Formation Bio is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome candidates from all backgrounds. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding, and related medical conditions), gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law. We've seen a rise in recruiting impersonation scams across the industry, where fake profiles pose as recruiters aiming to trick candidates into sharing personal and financial information through illegitimate interviews and job offers. All legitimate recruiting communications from Formation Bio will come from a @formation.bio http://formation.bio email address. If you receive outreach from someone claiming to work at Formation Bio through any other domain or channel, please disregard it and do not share any personal information.

jobs.title: Associate AI Engineer, OI&A
jobs.description: Career Category Sales & Marketing Operations Job Description Associate AI Engineer, OI&A Associate Data Scientist, Obesity Intelligence & Analytics What you will do Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. In this vital role, you’ll join a fun, innovative technology operations and data enablement team within the Obesity Intelligence & Analytics (OI&A) organization. You will deliver advanced data science, software engineering, and GenAI solutions that enable commercial and non-commercial functions across the enterprise. You will maintain technical continuity across the lifecycle, working with business stakeholders and multidisciplinary teams to shape the simplest viable solution, coordinate execution, make delivery trade-offs, remove blockers and contribute hands-on to critical components. The role combines enterprise solution engineering, applied AI/ML, GenAI, RAG and agents, integration, evaluation, MLOps/LLMOps, security, governance and production operations. Technical accountability complements, but does not replace, explicit product, business, compliance and long-term support ownership. Responsibilities Lead discovery by clarifying the business workflow, users, intended outcome, value hypothesis, acceptance criteria, operational constraints, data readiness, integration dependencies and production implications; Translate complex problems into an executable solution design, delivery plan, technical workstreams, estimates, milestones, dependencies, risks, acceptance criteria, release approach and support transition. Build, prototype, review or contribute to critical production components to prove feasibility or unblock delivery, including AI-enabled applications, RAG, bounded agents, intelligent automation, APIs and integrations. Define and maintain the integrated architecture across applications, workflows, data and knowledge pipelines, models, retrieval, agents, APIs, enterprise integrations, identity, access controls, observability and human review. Orchestrate delivery across full-stack software and AI engineering, data science, ML and context engineering, testing, platform, security, compliance and business roles; Establish integrated testing, AI evaluation and governance covering functional, performance, security, data, model, retrieval, generation, tool-use, human-oversight and operational behavior with explicit release thresholds. Coordinate production readiness through CI/CD, staged release, monitoring, logging, SLOs, rollback, recovery, runbooks and controlled deployment; support early issue triage, stabilization and transition to the operating owner. Communicate evidence, risks, trade-offs and status clearly; measure adoption and value and convert delivery lessons into reusable components, accelerators, standards, documentation and playbooks. What we expect of you We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The dynamic professional we seek is a collaborative professional with the following qualifications. Basic Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science or related field OR Diploma with 2+ years of experience in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or related field Preferred Qualifications: Enterprise solution architecture and integration: End-to-end design across applications, APIs, services, data and knowledge flows, models, retrieval, agents, workflows, persistence, identity, security zones, enterprise systems and support boundaries. Applied AI/ML and GenAI engineering: Production Python and SQL; classical ML and NLP awareness; foundation-model integration, prompt and context management, RAG, structured output, provenance, citations, bounded tool use, permissions, recovery and human control. Cloud, DevSecOps and lifecycle operations: Cloud-native services, containers, CI/CD, infrastructure as code, versioning, observability, SLOs, staged release, rollback, incidents, disaster recovery, capacity, FinOps, runbooks and MLOps/LLMOps. Strong hands-on proficiency in Python and SQL, with experience designing or reviewing production software, APIs, services, data flows, evaluation pipelines and enterprise integrations. Proven ability to turn complex business problems into coherent technical designs, executable delivery plans, acceptance criteria and production-readiness evidence while coordinating multidisciplinary teams. Advanced capability in at least one role-defining pillar—Applied AI/ML, GenAI/RAG/agents, full-stack and integration engineering, or AI platform/MLOps—plus credible breadth across the production lifecycle. Advanced RAG, knowledge and agent systems: Hybrid or graph retrieval, knowledge graphs, source verification, MCP-style integration, durable or multi-agent workflows, policy enforcement and adversarial testing. Experienced with Databricks, AWS, Spark, LLMs, and agentic development solutions is a plus. Additionally, experience in life sciences, healthcare, payor, or pharmaceutical environments will be factored in. Self-starter mentality: combines critical thinking, sound judgment, ownership, and resilience to navigate ambiguity, create clarity and momentum, and deliver business results with minimal oversight; provides credible, hands-on technical leadership through influence and constructive challenge; and communicates evidence, uncertainty, risks, trade-offs, limitations, and delivery status clearly while balancing value, speed, quality, security, maintainability across teams. What you can expect of us As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way. The expected annual salary range for this role in the U.S. (excluding Puerto Rico) is posted. Actual salary will vary based on several factors including but not limited to, relevant skills, experience, and qualifications. In addition to the base salary, Amgen offers a Total Rewards Plan, based on eligibility, comprising of health and welfare plans for staff and eligible dependents, financial plans with opportunities to save towards retirement or other goals, work/life balance, and career development opportunities that may include: A comprehensive employee benefits package, including a Retirement and Savings Plan with generous company contributions, group medical, dental and vision coverage, life and disability insurance, and flexible spending accounts A discretionary annual bonus program, or for field sales representatives, a sales-based incentive plan Stock-based long-term incentives Award-winning time-off plans Flexible work models where possible. Refer to the Work Location Type in the job posting to see if this applies. cold_email.subject: Interest in Associate AI Engineer, OI&A — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Amgen Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Associate AI Engineer, OI&A opportunity with Amgen at Amgen.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin
